axes_transform — ANNOTATE plot op

• Data kinds: none → axes (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.axes_transform(rect, xlim, ylim, invert_y=True, xscale='linear', yscale='linear') (to call the implementation directly, import annotate; annotate.axes_transform(rect, xlim, ylim, invert_y=True, xscale='linear', yscale='linear'); from the registry, opsannotate.get("axes_transform"))

Usage

Build the (closed-form) mapping from data coordinates to pixel coordinates.

The mismatch between the image fact row points down and the graph convention y points up is absorbed in this 1 place only. Figure code carries this dict around.

px = x0 + (x - xmin)/(xmax - xmin) * (w - 1)

py = y0 + (h - 1) - (y - ymin)/(ymax - ymin) * (h - 1) # invert_y

Parameters

rect : (x, y, w, h)

Drawing area (top-left origin, pixels).

xlim, ylim : (lo, hi)

Data range. lo == hi makes the slope infinite, so ValueError.

lo > hi (inverted axis) is also allowed -- for drawing depth or rank upside down.

invert_y : bool

If True (default), ylim[0] comes at the bottom edge = an ordinary graph.

If False, the image's own orientation (ylim[0] at the top edge).

xscale, yscale : {'linear','log'}

'log' is the common logarithm. If the range includes values at or below 0, ValueError

(a figure that passes 0 to a log axis and draws -inf as "the edge" is a lie).

Returns

dict

{"rect", "xlim", "ylim", "invert_y", "xscale", "yscale"}.

Raises

ValueError

invalid rectangle, range non-finite or of zero width, w or h below 2,

unknown scale, range at or below 0 on a log axis.
